```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(CellCycleDiag)
```

## Diagnose observed representations

```{r metadata}
meta <- data.frame(condition = rep(c("Control", "Treatment"), each = 4),
                   S.Score = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 2),
                   G2M.Score = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1),
                   theta = c(0, 0, pi, pi, 0, pi, pi, pi))
res <- diagnose_cc_imbalance(meta, "condition", "Control", "Treatment")
res
plot_cc_diagnostic(res)
```

The example is synthetic and illustrates the interface, not a biological result.
The expected D_score is 0.625 and D_theta is 0.25.

## Work from a Seurat object

```{r seurat, eval=FALSE}
seu <- add_cc_representation(seu, species = "human")
res <- diagnose_cc_imbalance(seu, "condition", "Control", "Treatment")
sens <- run_cc_sensitivity(seu, "condition", "Control", "Treatment",
                           donor.var = "donor")
sens$susceptibility
plot_cc_diagnostic(sens, "susceptibility")
```

Normalize expression beforehand and join split Seurat v5 data layers.
For mouse/ENSEMBL data supply matching phase gene sets explicitly.
MAST uses common baseline covariates in all three models and adds either
S/G2M scores or sin/cos of theta. This changes the DE model, not expression values.
Fixed donor effects do not make cells independent biological replicates.
Both-empty DEG sets yield undefined Jaccard distance, not evidence of robustness.

Variation, between-group imbalance and susceptibility are distinct concepts.
There is no recommended correction threshold. See function help for exact
mathematical conventions, input requirements and result fields.
